data.body:
CLOSING on Gerrit change 1121, whose Verified submit requirement is SATISFIED (operator +1 from
JoeOakhartNava; the rebar CI bot's -1 remains on the change, but Verified resolves on MAX VALUE, not
max-with-block — confirmed authoritatively via /changes/1121?o=SUBMIT_REQUIREMENTS returning
"Verified: SATISFIED"). Recording that explicitly because the aggregate LabelInfo still renders as
-1 and I initially misread that as a veto; the submit-requirement status is the authority, not the
aggregate.

WHY THE CI BOT VOTED -1 — recorded so nobody re-investigates it. Change 1121 fails EXACTLY ONE test,
tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py::test_runner_regains_real_headroom_under_the_cap, confirmed
from the GitHub Actions log rather than inferred; lint, typecheck and the module-size job all pass.
The cause is stack ORDER, not this ticket's content: cc33 adds +93 lines to runner.py on a 689-line
base (= 782), while task e6bd — the extraction that pays those lines back, taking runner.py to 699 —
sits ABOVE cc33 in the relation chain. Verified is cast PER PATCHSET, so no revision of THIS commit
can ever pass a guard its own content violates. That is a permanent property of this commit's
position, not a transient failure to retry.

REMEDIATION WAS EVALUATED AND DECLINED ON MEASURED GROUNDS, not waved away. Reordering e6bd below
cc33 does fix the arithmetic (689 -> 606 -> 699), and I probed it in a scratch worktree rather than
speculating: cherry-picking e6bd onto the pre-cc33 base produces FOUR conflict hunks in runner.py.
Two are trivial (an import block, a comment-wording block), but the hunks at ~392 and ~500 contain
cc33's OWN code — the "if fallback_targets:" branch and the model_scope / entered_fallback_model
ExitStack block — because e6bd was authored on a post-cc33 tree. Resolving them means re-authoring
the extraction against the older base, yielding a DIFFERENT e6bd commit from the one CI verified at
change 1123 and that ticket e6bd was closed on. The operator override was the cheaper and safer
path, and it is the case the standing per-firing rule was written for.

ACCEPTANCE: cc33's implementation was completed in an earlier session and is unchanged by any of the
above; this close is gated on Verified only. The full suite passes on the TOP of the stack (8237
passed / 74 skipped / 0 failed at change 1123), which exercises cc33's code with e6bd's extraction
applied — so cc33's behaviour is covered green even though its own intermediate patchset is not.

STILL OUTSTANDING FOR SUBMIT (not a blocker for this close): LLM-Review is UNSATISFIED on 1121, 1122,
1123 and 1128 — the review bot has voted only on 1119 and 1120. Submit needs LLM-Review +1 AND
Verified +1, so the stack is NOT landable yet even though this ticket's close criterion is met.
